newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: HORSE RACING-TOP JOCKEY BEADMAN QUITS FOR GOD.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-TOP JOCKEY BEADMAN QUITS FOR GOD.

text.p: Top Australian jockey Darren Beadman has announced he will quit horse racing at the peak of his career to become a Christian minister.
Beadman, 31, a two-time Melbourne Cup classic winner and a former national champion jockey, said he will retire in December to work full-time in an evangelical church.
"God told me it's an appropriate time to leave," said Beadman, winner of 1,108 races over the past 15 years.
"I get more pleasure and thrill from seeing people give their hearts to the Lord than winning a Melbourne Cup," Beadman told the Sydney Morning Herald newspaper on Monday.
Beadman last year guided the appropriately-named Saintly to victory in the Melbourne Cup handicap at Flemington, adding to his win on Kingston Rule in 1990.
But Saintly's veteran trainer Bart Cummings, a 10-time Melbourne Cup winner, said Beadman should seek a second opinion before making a final decision.

"He is at the top of his profession and one of the best ever," Cummings said. "To just drop out seems a severe move. Certainly Darren is dedicated to racing and it's a hard break to make, just to finish with the game."

Beadman said his experience in suriving two heavy falls several years ago in Hong Kong during one of his many overseas riding stints had persuaded him that God had intervened to save him. "I believe God looked after me," he said. "I was spearheaded into the ground and should have broken my neck."
